\textbf{Dual-Path Fusion.} To ground the frozen motion prior in the current scene, we encode the egocentric image into spatial tokens with DINOv3~\cite{dinov3} and process them through trainable root and body ControlNet branches. At selected layers of each Kimodo denoiser, we fuse visual context through two complementary paths. In the cross-attention path, future-motion hidden states serve as queries over the image tokens, allowing each predicted time step to retrieve task-relevant visual evidence. In parallel, a token-axis MLP maps the spatial image-token sequence to the future temporal horizon, providing a direct image-to-time correspondence. We sum the two outputs and pass them through a layer-specific zero-initialized projection to form a residual hint for the corresponding Kimodo layer. These hints are added only to future-motion tokens, leaving the constrained history prefix unchanged. Zero initialization preserves pretrained behavior at adaptation onset; the two paths support content-selective visual retrieval and temporally aligned conditioning.

\textbf{HandNet.} Hand control has different output semantics from root and body motion: it specifies when each hand should open or close, rather than a kinematic pose trajectory. We therefore model bilateral hand control with a dedicated diffusion head. At each denoising step, HandNet jointly processes the current hand state, noisy future hand controls, future body hidden states, and visual tokens, and predicts two hand-control values for every future frame. Conditioning on the predicted body and current scene aligns interaction commands with the evolving whole-body action, while a separate head avoids placing hand labels in the root--body motion space. The head supports binary open/close states and continuous closure changes. During training, body and visual features are detached: hand supervision updates HandNet, with no gradients to the motion denoiser or ControlNet.
